transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

For an earthy damp/musty smell, this is usually residue and bacteria build-up rather than a failed part. It collects in the rubber door seal, detergent drawer, drum and pump filter, especially with cool washes, excess detergent or when the machine is left shut. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Pull back the door-seal folds and wipe out any water, slime or mould. Clean the detergent drawer too. Black mould/slime supports a hygiene build-up.
2. With towels and a shallow tray ready, slowly open and clean the pump filter at the lower front, if accessible. Remove fluff, hair and debris, then refit it securely.
3. Run an empty 60–90°C maintenance wash using washing-machine cleaner or soda crystals, following the product directions. Do not put washing in with it.
4. Afterwards, leave the door and detergent drawer slightly ajar between washes, and use the recommended detergent amount rather than extra. If it is a sharp drains/rotten-egg smell, particularly strongest by the drain hose or after draining, the likely issue is the sink waste/standpipe trap or drain-hose installation rather than the washer-dryer. If it is hot, acrid or burning, stop using it and unplug it rather than running a cleaning cycle. Is the smell earthy/musty, like drains or rotten eggs, or hot/burning? Is there any black mould or slime in the door-seal folds or detergent drawer?

its a musty damp smell, not eggy or drainy and nothing burning. i had a look and theres black spots and grey sludge in the bottom fold of the door seal, and slimy black stuff in the softener bit of the drawer too

That visible black spotting, grey sludge and drawer slime make this a hygiene/biofilm build-up, rather than a failed washer-dryer part. The residue can transfer the musty smell back onto otherwise clean washing. 1. With the machine switched off and unplugged, thoroughly clean the seal folds and detergent drawer. Remove the drawer if it releases normally; rinse and scrub the softener compartment and its siphon cap/insert if fitted. Do not mix cleaning chemicals. 2. Next clean the pump filter: keep towels and a shallow tray ready, as water may come out. Remove any fluff or sludge, then refit it securely. A dirty filter can keep the odour going even after the seal and drawer look clean. 3. Do not add laundry, detergent or fabric softener to that cycle. 4. For prevention, use the detergent dose for your water/load rather than extra, avoid routinely overdosing softener, and leave both the door and drawer slightly ajar after use so the inside can dry. If the odour is still on clothes after this full clean and hot cycle, the next possibilities are residue deeper in the drum/filter system or, less likely given the smell type, a drainage installation issue. If the rubber seal is badly stained, cracked or perished and cannot be cleaned, an engineer can assess whether the door seal needs replacement.

Laundry left damp after an ineffective drying cycle (low)
